question_text: (a) Calculate the center-to-center separation distance of two Fe atoms along the $\langle 100\rangle$ direction in unstressed $\alpha$-iron (b) Calculate the separation distance along that direction under a tensile stress of $1,000 \mathrm{MPa}$. Give your answer as a tuple: (separation_distance_unstressed, separation_distance_stressed).The units of each required answer are (nm, nm), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

**Crystal structure:** α-iron (ferrite) is **BCC** with lattice parameter $a_0 \approx 0.2866\ \text{nm}$.

**(a) Unstressed separation along ⟨100⟩:**
In BCC, atoms sit at corners $(0,0,0)$ and body centers $(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$. A line in the $[100]$ direction through a corner atom passes through successive corner atoms at spacing $a_0$; the body-center atom (offset by $a/2$ in $y$ and $z$) does **not** lie on that line. Hence the nearest Fe–Fe separation along $\langle 100\rangle$ is simply the lattice parameter:

$$d_0 = a_0 = 0.2866\ \text{nm}$$

**(b) Under 1000 MPa tension along $[100]$:**
For a cubic crystal under uniaxial stress $\sigma_{xx}=\sigma$ along $[100]$ (all other stress components zero), the axial strain is

$$\varepsilon_{xx} = S_{11}\,\sigma, \qquad 
S_{11} = \frac{C_{11}+C_{12}}{(C_{11}-C_{12})(C_{11}+2C_{12})}$$

Using the elastic stiffnesses of α-Fe ($C_{11}=243,\ C_{12}=146,\ C_{44}=116$ GPa):

$$S_{11} = \frac{389}{(97)(535)} = 7.496\times10^{-3}\ \text{GPa}^{-1}$$

With $\sigma = 1000\ \text{MPa} = 1\ \text{GPa}$:

$$\varepsilon_{xx} = 7.496\times10^{-3}$$

$$d = a_0(1+\varepsilon_{xx}) = 0.2866\times1.007496 = 0.2887\ \text{nm}$$

The transverse strains ($S_{12}\sigma$) don't affect the $[100]$ spacing.

## Result

$$\boxed{(0.2866,\ 0.2887)}$$
